info.title: Stemmarest REST API
info.description:
Stemmarest is a Neo4j-based repository for variant text traditions (i.e. texts that have been transmitted in multiple manuscripts). For an introduction to its conceptual structure, read on; to dive into specific API calls, see the navigation menu, which is organised by the sort of object each call concerns.

### Definition of terms

What follows is a definition of the concepts that occur within Stemmarest; understanding these terms will be helpful for understanding the API documentation (each is also described again, in the same words, at the top of its own section in the navigation menu). Note that most of these entities are defined with respect to (therefore, under) the **/tradition/{tradId}** heading in the API; readings, although defined as root objects, always belong to one and only one tradition section.

tags.name: Tradition
tags.description: This is the central object in the database. A *tradition* represents the structure of our information about the text, from its witnesses to its sections to its readings and relations.

tags.name: User
tags.description: A *user* is an account that can own, create, and manage traditions.

tags.name: Witness
tags.description: A *witness* represents a document that carries some version of the text. Witnesses generally have *sigla* to identify them, and they can be assembled into one or more *stemma* hypotheses. The witness sigla are used to identify individual textual versions within the sections; there, witnesses may also have *layers* to represent changes made to the text in the document.

tags.name: Stemma
tags.description: A *stemma* (in this context more properly a *stemma hypothesis*) is a graph that asserts a particular set of copying relationships between *witnesses*. The witnesses in a stemma can be extant (meaning that their text appears in the tradition) or hypothetical (meaning that their text does not appear, and their existence is only conjectured based on the evidence of the copying history). The stemma objects in the database can have a *root* (or archetype), or not. The identity of the archetype can be changed by the user.

tags.name: Section
tags.description: The text of a tradition is divided into one or more *sections*, largely for manageability of the textual data. A section includes the set of *readings* from each *witness*, usually knitted together into a collation graph. Every section has a start node and an end node, and every witness (or, more precisely, every layer of every witness) takes a single path from the start to the end through a subset of the section's *readings*.

tags.name: Reading
tags.description: A *reading* is the base unit of the text. Most often this is equivalent to a word, but depending on context and on the needs of the editor, it may be a partial word, or it may be several words joined together. Readings are the nodes that are joined together by witness paths (a.k.a. sequences), and can be correlated by named *relations*. Two or more readings that are *colocated* in the collation (that is, they occupy the same place in the text, in different witnesses) are also known as *variants*.

tags.name: Relation
tags.description: It is often useful for an editor to be able to classify the types (or even the existence) of variation that occurs across witness texts. This is done via the *relation*, which (depending on its type; see below) usually also signals that the readings are *colocated*. They can also indicate correspondences such as *transposition* (when the same reading occurs in different places across different witnesses).

tags.name: Relation Type
tags.description: The user can define a set of *relation types* per tradition; these can be given unique names and arranged in a loose hierarchy.

tags.name: Annotation
tags.description: Arbitrary structured information can be added to any node in the tradition via the *annotation* framework. An annotation is a node that has user-defined properties, and user-defined outbound links (i.e. relationships) to specific sorts of nodes. An annotation framework is defined by means of *annotation labels* on the tradition.

tags.name: Annotation Label
tags.description: The *annotation label* defines a sort of annotation that may appear on the tradition, the properties it may contain, and the types of entities (i.e. nodes) that it may link to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the tradition. Default is the empty string.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: the ID of the user to whom this tradition belongs. Required.

parameters.name: public
parameters.description: If true, the tradition will be marked as publicly viewable.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: the language of the tradition text (e.g. Latin, Syriac).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: the direction in which the text should be read. Possible values are LR (left to right), RL (right to left), or BI (bidirectional). Default is LR.

parameters.name: empty
parameters.description: Should be set to some non-null value if the tradition is being created without any data file. Required if 'file' is not present.

parameters.name: filetype
parameters.description: the type of file being uploaded. Possible values are collatex, cxjson, csv, tsv, xls, xlsx, graphml, stemmaweb, or teips. Required if 'file' is present.

requestBody.description: Multipart form data for the tradition upload.

400.description: No file was specified, and the 'empty' flag was not set.

409.description: The requested owner does not exist in the database.

500.description: Something went wrong. An error message will be returned.

direction.description: Direction of the tradition (LR, RL, or BI)

is_public.description: Whether the tradition should be viewable by other users

owner.description: User ID of the tradition's owner

witnesses.description: The list of witness sigla belonging to this tradition

items.description: The list of witness sigla belonging to this tradition

id.description: The internal (application-managed, numeric) ID of the stemma.

name.description: The name of the stemma. Must be unique within a tradition.

is_undirected.description: True if this is an undirected tree, rather than a directed stemma.

is_contaminated.description: True if the stemma indicates witness contamination / conflation.

dot.description: A string that holds the dot specification of the stemma or tree topology.

newick.description: A string that holds the Newick specification of the tree topology.
